messages:
Chris Osei: dropping early readout for the Hosted self-serve pricing experiment (credits + overage tiers). tl;dr: Variant B looks like +8–10% paid conversion but churn ticked up in week 3. I’m not 100% confident we’re reading it right bc cohort mix shifted. link to sheet (wip): https://drive.google.com/redwood/pricing-exp-readout-wip

Nikhil Sharma: thx. my immediate worry: Variant B got a ton of “AI demo week” signups (high-intent) + we also changed the onboarding email sequence mid-run. feels like we’re attributing too much to pricing.

Mei Lin: +1 on mix shift. I pulled a quick breakdown: B has 22% more “first request within 10 min of signup” users vs A. That’s huge. Not sure if randomization got skewed by the eligibility rule?

Chris Osei: eligibility is “new orgs only, hosted only, USD billing country.” randomization happens at org_create. but we also excluded anyone w/ referral code (partnerships) starting Jan 29. That might be what you’re seeing.

Isabelle Laurent: from sales side: some of those “AI demo week” signups are actually coming from AE outbound + then they self-serve before we can convert to CRM. so they look self-serve but they’re not “typical.” :grimacing:

Rishi Malhotra: if B is pulling in higher-intent leads, that’s fine if we can replicate. question is: does it generalize and what’s margin impact? early calc in the sheet assumes same token mix, but B users are heavier on larger models + lower cache hit rate.

Sana Farid: I skimmed the sheet. A couple stats notes:
- The conversion lift is directionally positive but current p-value is not stable bc you’re peeking daily + not using a sequential test.
- The churn signal is super noisy (short window). We should not call “higher churn” off week-3 cancel unless we control for usage level + account type.
- Biggest issue: selection/censoring. Anyone who hits the free credit cap early will “convert” mechanically. Need to look at *net revenue per signup* and *retained revenue after 30 days*, not just conversion.

Nikhil Sharma: +1000. also are we counting “converted” as adding a card or actually paying invoice? because some add card then never exceed credits.

Chris Osei: definition in the sheet is “adds payment method OR signs paid plan.” I can split: add_card vs first_paid_invoice.

Mei Lin: another potential bias: we had that usage reporting delay incident on Feb 2–3. Some people might have hit the cap but didn’t see it in-console, then got surprised by overage later. That could affect churn/support tickets.

Rishi Malhotra: yup, and from finance perspective we saw a small spike in goodwill credits right after that (not sure if tied). We should tag accounts that got credits/refunds and exclude or analyze separately.

Evelyn Hart: what decision do we need this week? extend/stop/ship? I need a recommendation for exec staff on Friday.

Chris Osei: currently scheduled to end Feb 9. question is whether to extend 1 more cycle to get cleaner read (and maybe update eligibility) vs make call now.

Sana Farid: extending is reasonable IF we fix the analysis plan first. Right now the primary metric is too easy to game by the free-credit design.

Nikhil Sharma: what would “fix” mean without changing the product mid-test? we can’t change credits again or we’ll invalidate.

Sana Farid: we can keep variants as-is but:
1) lock an analysis window + stop peeking (or use sequential boundaries)
2) pre-specify segmentation (self-serve true vs sales-assisted; model family; region)
3) use “revenue per eligible signup @ 14/30 days” as primary, with guardrails for support tickets + refund rate
4) exclude (or mark) cohorts impacted by onboarding email change + console incident

Chris Osei: makes sense. re: “sales-assisted”: how do we identify? CRM association is messy.

Isabelle Laurent: we can approximate: if domain matches an open HubSpot company record OR if they used an enterprise email + hit the “talk to sales” CTA. Not perfect. I can pull a list of domains from HubSpot for the last 30 days.

Mei Lin: I can join on domain + also look at “used sales token” events (demo API keys we hand out). there’s an internal tag on orgs created from AE links.

Rishi Malhotra: if we extend, can we add a guardrail on GM? like “do not ship if margin drops >X pts.” B seems to push more traffic to high-cost models (people burn credits on bigger stuff).

Nikhil Sharma: that’s a product question too: is the goal conversion at any cost or unit economics neutral? I assumed we needed conversion without materially increasing CAC or COGS per signup.

Evelyn Hart: goal is profitable growth. If B converts but drives bad workloads / high support / refund, it’s not a win.

Chris Osei: ok so proposal:
- extend 1 more cycle (2 weeks) but freeze variant configs
- tighten analysis plan (Sana + me)
- add segments for sales-assisted + exclude known incident window
- readout on Feb 23 w/ recommendation

Sana Farid: I’m good w/ that as long as we agree in writing what “win” is. also please stop showing the “+10% conversion” number in the weekly email until we adjust. it’s misleading.

Nikhil Sharma: +1. I can message #product-growth to temper the narrative.

Rishi Malhotra: also: please add a view for “net $ after credits” (realized revenue) and “expected GPU cost” so we get contribution margin per signup. I can help w/ the cost model inputs.

Mei Lin: + I’ll rerun the cohort table with: signup week, first_request_latency bucket, region, model_family. Should show whether randomization is drifting.

Isabelle Laurent: I’ll send Chris a domain list + tag likely sales-assisted. (will be incomplete but better than nothing)

Evelyn Hart: action items + owner list please. and I want a 1-paragraph rationale for extending (what uncertainty we’re resolving).

Chris Osei: will do. posting here:
- Chris: update analysis plan + revise readout metrics (add_card vs paid_invoice; rev/signup; refund rate) by Wed
- Sana: sanity check stats approach + recommend sequential vs fixed-horizon by Wed
- Mei: cohort mix / randomization drift analysis by Thu
- Isabelle: sales-assisted domain list + heuristics by Thu
- Rishi: margin model overlay + guardrail proposal by Fri

Chris Osei: rationale for extend: current readout confounded by (1) onboarding email change, (2) eligibility rule tweak (referral exclusion), (3) console/usage delay incident. extending gives a clean post-change cohort + enough time for invoices/overage to settle.

Sana Farid: :thumbsup: also please note that if we extend, we should keep sample size target + stop date fixed to avoid infinite running.

Evelyn Hart: approved to extend pending sanity check that we’re not creating customer harm. add support ticket volume as a guardrail.

Nikhil Sharma: will ping Dev/Support for ticket counts + themes. If we see “surprise overage” complaints, we may need to pause.

Chris Osei: cool. I’ll update the experiment registry + comms.
